headline: Touchscreen MacBook rumored for next week, taking cues from Lenovo's Yoga 9n
summary: The rumored touchscreen MacBook could learn from Lenovo's Yoga 9n, a 2-in-1 convertible with a stylus that works on both its OLED screen and haptic trackpad, offering versatile input options.
details: The long-rumored touchscreen MacBook is reportedly set for an announcement next week, with tech enthusiasts looking to the Lenovo Yoga 9n as a potential source of inspiration for Apple's design.

The Lenovo Yoga 9n features an Arm-based processor with a powerful integrated GPU and unified memory, similar to Apple silicon. It stands out as a 16-inch 2-in-1 convertible laptop, equipped with a stylus.

This convertible design allows the Yoga 9n to function as a traditional clamshell laptop, or fold into tent and tablet modes. This versatility is ideal for watching movies, gaming with a controller, or integrating into a multi-monitor setup.

Its included stylus enhances usability for note-taking and drawing on the excellent OLED display. Uniquely, it also works on the haptic trackpad, providing a Wacom-like experience without obstructing the screen.

The stylus attaches magnetically to the Yoga's lid for convenience and relies on USB-C for charging. This feature is particularly useful for tasks like photo retouching in applications such as Lightroom Classic or Photoshop.

Hopes are high that a touchscreen MacBook Pro would support the Apple Pencil, ideally with both screen and trackpad functionality. Magnetic attachment with wireless charging, similar to the iPad Pro, would also be a significant convenience upgrade.

Apple is expected to deliver a unique take on the touchscreen laptop, possibly akin to Microsoft's Surface Laptop Studio, rather than a standard 2-in-1. Hints in macOS 27 (Golden Gate) suggest updates to make touch interactions more natural and intuitive.

Anticipation is high for Apple to innovate, especially given the expected premium price of a touch-enabled MacBook Pro. Past design decisions, like the butterfly keyboard, highlight the importance of a flawless execution for this new venture.

headline: AI agents can now live in your text messages, performing tasks and remembering context
summary: Instead of downloading new apps, these AI agents can be texted like a person, connecting to your existing services to schedule, research, shop, and more.
details: A growing number of AI agents can be texted like ordinary people, eliminating the need for new app downloads. They remember context and connect to existing apps and services to complete tasks on your behalf.

These tasks include scheduling appointments, organizing calendars, researching trips, sending emails, making reservations, and online shopping. Instinct is a buzzy agent, valued at $10 billion after a $1 billion funding round.

Ask Proxy differentiates itself by "thinking like a woman," aiming to anticipate user needs proactively. It functions as a chatbot via SMS for gift ideas, event planning, or daily decisions, and can even interpret photos for tasks like decorating.

Ask Proxy also offers a work-focused version designed to boost employee productivity while keeping personal data off company systems. The personal version costs $1 per day, with business pricing starting at $15 per employee per month.

Caddy is an AI assistant for iMessage and RCS that organizes information from your phone into actionable items. It connects to calendars and conversations to identify tasks, add events, set reminders, and conduct research without a separate app.
Comma manages tasks across work and daily life, ensuring completion and surfacing work for review when approval is needed. It proactively notifies users and recommends next steps.

Comma works across browsers, computers, and files, accessible remotely via messaging apps like Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. It maintains context and memory across devices, providing daily briefings, urgent flags, and call summaries.

Fambot acts as an AI "chief of staff" for families, organizing school communications, activities, meal planning, and calendars. It works via an app and SMS, sending daily summaries of upcoming events and to-dos.

Fambot connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with Apple Calendar support planned. Launched in beta in September 2026, it raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding and is currently free, with future plans for a Netflix-like subscription fee.
Folk is another AI assistant accessible through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram, designed to remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, and track flights.
